advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm intended behavior when write_lock_is_busy() encounters a stale/orphaned lock dir (dead holder) that acquire() would reclaim — the probe currently reports 'busy', deferring compaction on an effectively-free store.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/lock.py:346: `os.mkdir(lock_dir)` then `except FileExistsError: return True` — no _mkdir_lock_is_stale check, unlike _acquire_mkdir at src/rebar/_store/lock.py:622-624 which reclaims a provably-stale dir

tests/unit/test_write_lock_busy_probe_7084.py: `# The killed holder leaves its mkdir stamp behind, so the store still reads busy` then `assert _lock.write_lock_is_busy(str(tmp_path)) is True` — confirms the probe returns busy on an orphan acquire() would reclaim
transition_close.py docstring: `a false "busy" just defers optional work` understates that a crashed-writer orphan defers it repeatedly, not momentarily
advisory.finding: write_lock_is_busy() reports 'busy' for a stale/orphaned mkdir lock (dead holder) that acquire() would reclaim and succeed on, because the probe omits the _mkdir_lock_is_stale/reclaim path that _acquire_mkdir runs. Compact-on-close is therefore skipped on a store that is effectively free whenever a previous writer crashed leaving its lock dir, potentially until the 1h stale ceiling.
scenarios: A prior write process crashes/is killed holding the lock, leaving an orphan .ticket-write.lock.d; every subsequent close-of-ticket skips compaction until the orphan is reclaimed by a real acquire or the stale ceiling expires.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a unit test monkeypatching os.mkdir to raise a non-EEXIST OSError and asserting write_lock_is_busy returns False (mkdir-leg fail-open).
evidence: Unit suite tests fcntl fail-open (test_probe_fails_open_on_an_unexpected_error, ENOLCK) and os.open fail-open (test_probe_fails_open_when_the_lock_file_cannot_be_opened, EACCES) but has no monkeypatch of os.mkdir raising a non-EEXIST OSError.

ABSENCE: a regression turning the mkdir non-EEXIST branch into `return True` would suppress compaction on a genuinely free store, matching the exact failure the docstring says fail-open must prevent, yet no test would catch it.
advisory.finding: The mkdir-leg fail-open branch of write_lock_is_busy (a non-EEXIST OSError from os.mkdir returns 'not busy') has no test, while both fcntl fail-open paths are covered — leaving the probe's documented fail-open contract only half-verified on the mkdir leg.
